findings.finding: Gold has surged past USD 4 000 per troy ounce (Oct-2025) as investors—especially non-Western central banks—seek “out-of-system” assets amid fiscal dominance and the weaponisation of the Western financial system.

evidence.quote: It broke through the USD 4000 per troy ounce threshold in mid-October before entering a consolidation phase.
Gold’s remarkable ascent … is fundamentally supported by structural demand for physically backed gold financial instruments, particularly from non-Western central banks.

findings.finding: Swiss franc–denominated assets (equities, real estate) are highlighted as strategic store-of-value holdings that can diversify portfolios and protect against confiscatory policies in a multipolar world.

evidence.quote: In a multipolar world, Swiss assets – anchored by the safe-haven CHF – offer investors … store-of-value protection and enhanced diversification.
Switzerland’s public sector remains among the least indebted globally … reinforcing the CHF’s safe-haven status and supporting its long-term appreciation.

findings.finding: Western central banks rapidly raised rates in 2022-23 and have already pivoted to easing; the U.S. Fed cut 150 bp by Nov-2025, yet debate persists on whether rates will revert to pre-2020 lows.

evidence.quote: Faced with an inflation spike for the first time in decades, Western central banks have rapidly reset the cost of capital in the system.
By November 2025, the federal funds rate had been lowered by a cumulative 150 basis points … to 3.75%–4%.

findings.finding: The innovation super-cycle is led by AI hyperscalers driving record data-centre capex; power availability has become the critical bottleneck, making energy ‘the new currency’.

evidence.quote: US equity markets, led by AI hyperscalers, have surged to new highs, fuelling an unprecedented capex cycle … spending on data centres is now close to overtaking investment in new office buildings in the US.
If 2025 made anything clear, it is this: in the race to scale AI, energy is the new currency.

findings.finding: Chinese policy is engineering a managed domestic equity bull market to repair household balance sheets; conditions for the first secular Chinese equity bull market are ‘slowly falling into place’.

evidence.quote: This should incentivise Chinese households to shift some of their savings into equities … A managed and sustainable domestic equity bull market would, in turn, help restore depressed consumer confidence.
We believe the conditions for the first secular – rather than cyclical – equity bull market in China are slowly falling into place.

findings.finding: Europe has embraced fiscal activism: Germany’s historic infrastructure/defence U-turn and NATO’s new 5 %-of-GDP defence target signal lasting expansionary policy.

evidence.quote: Germany’s historic fiscal and defence U-turn … could prove to be a turning point.
Member nations committed to a new defence spending target amounting to 5% of GDP by 2035, more than double the previous 2% guideline.

findings.finding: Private-sector balance sheets in the U.S. are strong after years of deleveraging, while public-sector debt service costs now exceed defence spending, underscoring fiscal dominance risks.

evidence.quote: US households have moved from balance sheet recession to balance sheet strength, more than doubling their net wealth …
Today, the US has reached a tipping point where it spends more on interest payments on its federal debt than on defence.

findings.finding: Key global risks identified include climate change, cyber threats, dormant systemic risk in shadow banking, geopolitical conflicts, and infrastructure vulnerabilities.

evidence.quote: Growing climate, cyber, and geopolitical threats – alongside systemic vulnerabilities and infrastructure weaknesses – are heightening global economic risks.
